headline: Your bench is beating your starters
summary: This is the most fixable 0–2 in the league, and I mean that kindly. You've left 66.5 points on your bench in two weeks — 53.68 of them in week 1 — which is the worst in the league. You don't need new players. You have Malik Nabers, ranked WR15, sitting on your bench while a receiver ranked WR37 starts. Move three names and this team looks completely different.

waivers.why: Justin Jefferson hurt his ankle on Sunday, which promotes Addison to his team's number one receiver. He already got a 41-yard touchdown out of it. But be honest with yourself: this is a nice-to-have. Your actual problem is who you're starting.
waivers.stat: Ranked WR50 for the rest of the season, which is stale — that was before Jefferson got hurt.

start_sit.why: Nabers is ranked WR15. Boston is WR37. Nabers has had two quiet weeks and it is still not close — he led his team in targets on Sunday, which means the ball is going his way even when the yards aren't there yet. Start him.
Maye is ranked QB11, Young is QB16. You have the better quarterback on your bench. There's no story here, just swap them.
If you only make one change, make it Nabers. But Metcalf (WR35) also just scored a touchdown and outranks Boston, and he gets a friendlier matchup this week.

watch.note: On injured reserve with a heel problem. He is not playing, so he's your free drop whenever you want one.
Ruled OUT for the second week in a row with a hamstring. Could miss more time — don't count on him.
Getting the carries, but on an offence that can't score. Playable in a pinch, not someone to build around.

trade_ideas.why: Samantha just lost both of her starting running backs — one to a torn ACL, one ruled out — and she is desperate. You have Jonathan Taylor, Chase Brown, Chuba Hubbard and Aaron Jones already. This is the week her price is lowest.

your_habits.title: Points left behind
your_habits.text: 66.5 points benched in two weeks, the most in the league. Your week 1 bench alone outscored your starters by 53.68 — you scored 95.12 and lost by 16.44.

your_habits.title: Not actually unlucky
your_habits.text: Your 'vs. everyone' record is 1–13, so this isn't the schedule. It's the lineup, and the lineup is the one thing entirely in your control.

glossary.def: The best possible score you could have had if you'd known in advance which of your players would do well. Nobody hits it, but the gap is worth watching.
A roster list for players who are hurt long-term. Someone on IR is not playing, so holding them is usually a wasted spot.
Passes thrown in a receiver's direction, caught or not. A receiver getting lots of targets is being trusted, and the points usually follow.
Who your player's real NFL team is playing. A great receiver against a great defence can have a quiet day.
What your record would be against all seven teams every week. It separates bad luck from bad decisions.
